pathways.title: Strata and community scheme disputes
pathways.scope: Choose the particular order first: mediation requirements depend on the order sought.

steps.action: Attempt strata mediation.
steps.before: Before lodging an NCAT application for an order requiring mediation.
steps.evidence: Mediation certificate or evidence supporting the specific exemption.
steps.timing: Check the time limit for the particular order.

steps.action: Apply for an order within NCAT’s jurisdiction.
steps.before: You must be an eligible applicant, identify the order and statutory provision, and satisfy mediation or an exemption.
steps.evidence: Application, scheme details, relevant records and mediation evidence.
steps.timing: Order-specific limits apply; consult the orders table.

pathways.exceptions: Some orders bypass mediation, including specified appointment, access, penalty and records orders. The statutory exemptions and orders table control; urgent circumstances must be assessed under the actual rule.

pathways.title: NSW administrative decision review
pathways.scope: Only decisions made reviewable by an enabling law can be reviewed by NCAT.

steps.action: Request internal review of the decision.
steps.before: Before NCAT administrative review where the enabling law requires it.
steps.evidence: Decision, notification date, request, reasons and supporting material.
steps.timing: Generally request internal review within 28 days of being told of the original decision; check the specific law.

steps.action: Apply for administrative review.
steps.before: A reviewable decision, standing and internal review or an applicable exception are required.
steps.evidence: Original and internal-review decisions, proof of dates, relevant evidence and requested outcome.
steps.timing: Generally 28 days after notification of the internal-review decision; check exceptions and extensions.

pathways.exceptions: The particular enabling law may exempt internal review. NCAT is not a general appeal body for every government action.

pathways.title: Privacy: NSW public sector agency → NCAT
pathways.scope: This is the NSW public-sector internal-review route, not the private-sector or Commonwealth privacy route.

steps.action: Make a valid written privacy internal-review application.
steps.before: NCAT requires a valid internal-review application to the agency first.
steps.evidence: Conduct complained of, when you became aware, supporting material and Australian postal/email address.
steps.timing: Normally within 6 months of awareness; agency may accept a later application.

steps.action: Seek review of the conduct covered by the internal-review application.
steps.before: Internal-review outcome received, or review not completed within 60 days of receipt.
steps.evidence: Application, proof of receipt, outcome or evidence of elapsed time.
steps.timing: Apply within 28 days of the report, or within 28 days after the 60-day period ends if unfinished.

pathways.exceptions: A complaint to the Privacy Commissioner does not itself provide this NCAT review right. Later conduct may need a separate application.

pathways.title: Government information: alternative review routes
pathways.scope: Internal review, Information Commissioner review and NCAT review are alternatives with conditions, not a compulsory three-stage ladder.

steps.action: Identify a reviewable GIPA decision and your status as applicant or third party.
steps.before: The original access applicant can often approach IPC or NCAT without internal review; third-party requirements differ.
steps.evidence: Access application, decision, notification date and reasons for disagreement.
steps.timing: IPC: 40 working days; NCAT generally 40 working days, or 20 working days following IPC review outcome. Check the source for the chosen route.

pathways.exceptions: Third parties must seek internal review before NCAT where available. IPC cannot review its own access decision; special Supreme Court leave requirements affect NCAT review of IPC decisions. Parallel/completed NCAT review restricts IPC review.

pathways.title: NSW discrimination complaint → referral → NCAT
pathways.scope: NSW Anti-Discrimination Act pathway; Commonwealth discrimination procedures are separate.

steps.action: Lodge a complaint within the agency’s legal coverage.
steps.before: The agency assesses, investigates and may conciliate the complaint.
steps.evidence: Account of events, relevant dates, parties, protected ground and area of public life.
steps.timing: Check complaint acceptance time limits and any discretion.

steps.action: Participate in the referred complaint proceeding.
steps.before: The complaint must be referred through the statutory Anti-Discrimination NSW process.
steps.evidence: Referral letter, President’s Report, response and supporting evidence.
steps.timing: Follow NCAT’s case-conference notice and directions.

pathways.exceptions: Not every unfair action falls within discrimination law. A declined complaint has its own statutory process; do not treat every complaint as directly fileable in NCAT.

pathways.title: Centrelink decision → formal review → ART
pathways.scope: Review of a Centrelink decision is different from a service complaint.

steps.action: Request formal review of the decision.
steps.before: Identify the particular decision and review rights.
steps.evidence: Decision, date received, reasons and supporting documents.
steps.timing: Check the decision-specific time limit and effects on back payment.

steps.action: Apply to review the ARO decision.
steps.before: ART usually requires an ARO review first; the particular decision must be reviewable.
steps.evidence: ARO decision, original decision and supporting evidence.
steps.timing: Check the applicable ART deadline on the decision and source.

pathways.exceptions: An informal explanation or general complaint is not the same as an ARO review. Some decisions have different review rules.

pathways.title: NDIA decision → internal review → ART
pathways.scope: Reviewable NDIA decisions affecting participants or applicants.

steps.action: Request internal review of a reviewable decision.
steps.before: Identify the decision and why it should change.
steps.evidence: Decision, date received, reasons and disability/support evidence.
steps.timing: Request within 3 months of receiving the decision.

steps.action: Apply for external review if you disagree with the internal-review decision.
steps.before: An internal-review decision and eligibility to seek review.
steps.evidence: Internal-review decision and evidence supporting your position.
steps.timing: Normally 28 days from the day after receiving the written internal-review decision; extension may be available.

pathways.exceptions: Urgent or delayed decisions and extensions need their own assessment. A service complaint is not a substitute for decision review.

pathways.title: Unfair dismissal: identify system → apply → Commission process
pathways.scope: National-system FWC route. NSW state-system employment may instead fall within the NSW IRC.

steps.action: Check coverage, minimum employment period and other eligibility, then lodge.
steps.before: Dismissal must have taken effect and unfair-dismissal eligibility must be met.
steps.evidence: Dismissal date, employment details, dismissal letter and reasons.
steps.timing: Within 21 days after dismissal takes effect; extensions only in exceptional circumstances.

steps.action: Follow conciliation and hearing directions.
steps.before: An application has commenced the legal process.
steps.evidence: Application, employer response, notices and relevant evidence.
steps.timing: Use the case notices; an employer/FWO complaint does not replace timely filing.

pathways.exceptions: Do not wait for a general complaint process to finish before protecting a filing deadline. Check NSW IRC eligibility separately: https://irc.nsw.gov.au/claims-and-applications/unfair-dismissal.html

pathways.title: Financial firm → AFCA
pathways.scope: AFCA’s membership, subject-matter and time-limit rules determine coverage.

steps.action: Raise the complaint with the firm and state the outcome sought.
steps.before: Normally give the firm an opportunity to resolve it.
steps.evidence: Complaint, delivery date, account/product records and response.
steps.timing: Check product-specific response and AFCA filing limits.

steps.action: Bring an unresolved complaint to AFCA.
steps.before: AFCA checks member-firm and complaint coverage; it may refer information to the firm to resolve first.
steps.evidence: Firm details, complaint, response, relevant documents and requested outcome.
steps.timing: Check current AFCA rules, including urgent circumstances and limits.

pathways.exceptions: Contact AFCA about urgent circumstances or difficulty using the firm’s process; do not invent a universal waiting period.

pathways.title: Health care complaint → HCCC
pathways.scope: Complaint about a NSW health service or practitioner within HCCC coverage.

steps.action: Submit a complaint or contact HCCC for assistance.
steps.before: Identify the provider and concern; a provider complaint is not presented here as a universal prerequisite.
steps.evidence: Account, relevant dates, provider details and available supporting records.
steps.timing: Read current complaint and consent requirements.

pathways.exceptions: Treatment orders, compensation claims and professional disciplinary proceedings follow different jurisdictions. HCCC assessment does not itself give a complainant a general right to bring disciplinary proceedings in NCAT.

pathways.title: NSW agency/service complaint → NSW Ombudsman
pathways.scope: For an agency, council or funded service within the Ombudsman’s oversight.

steps.action: Explain concerns through the organisation’s complaint process.
steps.before: Before escalation, normally give the organisation an opportunity to respond.
steps.evidence: Complaint, correspondence, dates, response and outcome sought.
steps.timing: Keep the complaint timeline and any promised response dates.

steps.action: Ask the Ombudsman to consider the unresolved complaint.
steps.before: The body and issue must fall within oversight; provide earlier communications.
steps.evidence: Copies of communication with the agency and its response, or explain obstacles to contacting it.
steps.timing: Check current acceptance requirements; protect any separate review/appeal deadline.

pathways.exceptions: Explain barriers to complaining directly. Ombudsman oversight is not a merits appeal and does not automatically replace statutory review.

pathways.title: Home building dispute → complaint investigation → NCAT
pathways.scope: NSW residential building jurisdiction; check the current Building Commission NSW/Fair Trading entry point.

steps.body: Building Commission NSW / NSW Fair Trading
steps.action: Refer the building dispute through the applicable investigation/dispute process.
steps.before: Before NCAT accepts a non-exempt claim.
steps.evidence: Investigation/rectification correspondence, contract, insurance, licence and building evidence.
steps.timing: Check the deadline for the particular claim; imminent expiry is among listed exceptions.

steps.action: Apply with the proper respondent and orders sought.
steps.before: Investigation evidence or a specified exemption; claim within jurisdiction and time.
steps.evidence: Contract, reports, correct legal entity/service address and investigation evidence.
steps.timing: Depends on the order and Home Building Act; consult the official source.

pathways.exceptions: Listed exemptions include insurer appeals, contractor debt claims, cross-claims, expiry within 3 months and specified contractor/company circumstances. Check the full official list.

pathways.title: Tenancy: select the order → meet its conditions → NCAT
pathways.scope: A repair, bond, termination, compensation or rent order has its own prerequisites.

steps.action: Find the precise order, who can apply, statutory provision, notice and time limit.
steps.before: Use the requirements for that order; do not import strata mediation rules into tenancy.
steps.evidence: Lease, notices, correspondence, rent/bond records or repair evidence relevant to the order.
steps.timing: The orders table gives different periods for different orders.

steps.action: Lodge the tenancy application with the order-specific evidence.
steps.before: Eligible applicant, jurisdiction, required notices and order-specific time limits.
steps.evidence: Application, correct respondent and documents proving required earlier steps.
steps.timing: Check the selected order; urgent matters need the applicable urgent procedure.

pathways.exceptions: Social-housing allocation/eligibility appeals and landlord–tenant disputes are different pathways. Do not treat all housing issues as NCAT tenancy claims.

pathways.title: Parenting orders: dispute resolution or exemption → Court
pathways.scope: Applications for parenting orders under Commonwealth family law.

steps.action: Obtain a valid section 60I certificate or establish a recognised exemption.
steps.before: Before filing the parenting application unless the Court accepts an exemption.
steps.evidence: Certificate or affidavit explaining the exemption, plus required court documents.
steps.timing: Check pre-filing requirements for the actual application.

steps.action: File the parenting application with certificate or exemption request.
steps.before: Meet applicable pre-action and filing requirements.
steps.evidence: Application, required affidavits/notices and certificate or exemption material.
steps.timing: Urgent matters and risk situations have specific procedures.

pathways.exceptions: Family violence, child abuse, urgency and other statutory grounds may support exemption. Do not require unsafe mediation. Divorce and property applications have different prerequisites.

pathways.title: Local Court criminal decision → District Court appeal
pathways.scope: Conviction/sentence appeal route, not a police conduct complaint.

steps.requirement: Existing decision required; leave in specified cases
steps.action: Lodge a Notice of Appeal identifying the decision and grounds.
steps.before: A relevant Local Court decision; conviction appeals after a guilty plea require leave.
steps.evidence: Orders, decision date, grounds and application for leave where required.
steps.timing: Normally 28 days; up to 3 months with District Court leave.

pathways.exceptions: Advice should address harsher-penalty/cost risks. This deadline is not a rule for every court or every kind of appeal.

pathways.title: After NCAT: check appeal rights → leave if needed → correct forum
pathways.scope: Only an appealable decision can go to the Internal Appeal Panel; some matters have a different appeal route.

steps.action: Check appealability, grounds, leave requirements and the applicable deadline before lodging.
steps.before: An appealable NCAT decision; merits grounds generally need leave.
steps.evidence: Decision, reasons, notification dates, grounds and requested orders.
steps.timing: General rule 28 days; residential proceedings generally 14 days. Other enabling-law periods may apply.

steps.requirement: Only if a right or review jurisdiction exists
steps.action: Identify the actual statutory appeal or judicial-review basis.
steps.before: No second internal NCAT appeal from an Appeal Panel decision; Court access depends on jurisdiction, grounds, leave and time.
steps.evidence: Decision, reasons, grounds and documents required by the applicable Court process.
steps.timing: Check the Court rules and enabling law; do not reuse an NCAT deadline.

pathways.exceptions: An appeal does not automatically stay an order. A stay, set-aside, variation, enforcement and judicial review are distinct procedures.

registers.title: NSW legislation: all in-force Acts, regulations and historical versions
